job.title: People & Culture Business Partner
job.description:
The Opportunity
An established Australian family owned organisation with a national footprint is seeking an experienced People & Culture Business Partner to support its South Australian business.

This is a broad, hands-on HR partnering role offering considerable autonomy and exposure across the full employee lifecycle. Working closely with senior leaders and as part of a national People & Culture function, you will act as the key P&C contact for the South Australian business, balancing strategic partnering with the delivery of pragmatic, commercially focused HR solutions.

The environment is fast-paced and operational, so this opportunity will suit someone who enjoys being close to the business, building credibility with leaders and employees, and taking ownership rather than operating within a highly segmented HR model.

The Role
Partnering with leaders across the business, you will provide advice, coaching and support across a diverse range of people matters. You will build trusted stakeholder relationships and help strengthen leadership capability while ensuring national people initiatives are effectively embedded locally.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Providing operational HR advice and coaching to leaders across the employee lifecycle.
  • Managing complex employee and industrial relations matters, including workplace investigations and performance issues.
  • Playing an active role in enterprise bargaining, including preparation, stakeholder engagement, and implementation.
  • Supporting workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding and retention strategies.
  • Coaching leaders on performance management, development and effective people leadership.
  • Supporting organisational change and transformation initiatives.
  • Providing guidance on employment legislation, industrial instruments, policies and procedures.
  • Contributing to the development and implementation of broader national People & Culture projects and initiatives.
  • Using workforce insights and data to identify trends and support better people and business decisions.
About You
You will be an experienced HR generalist who is comfortable operating autonomously and can move confidently between strategic conversations and hands-on employee matters.

Ideally, you will bring:
  • 3+ years' experience in an HR Business Partner or comparable generalist HR position.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Business Management or a related discipline.
  • Sound knowledge of Australian employment legislation, workplace relations and contemporary HR practices.
  • Practical experience managing employee relations and industrial relations matters.
  • The confidence to coach and influence leaders at different levels of an organisation.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication and relationship-building capability.
  • The ability to navigate change, ambiguity and sensitive workplace matters with sound judgement.
  • A commercial and pragmatic approach, with the ability to use data and insights to inform decisions.
  • The ability to work independently while remaining closely connected to a broader national HR team.
Experience within transport, logistics, manufacturing, warehousing, infrastructure, engineering or another operational/industrial environment would be particularly valuable.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is an excellent opportunity for an HR professional looking for genuine ownership and breadth. Rather than specialising in one area of HR, you will work closely with the business across the full spectrum of people matters, while having access to the expertise and support of a national P&C function.

You will have the opportunity to guide and influence leaders, navigate ER/IR matters, contribute to enterprise bargaining and change initiatives, and help shape the people agenda within the South Australian operation.

If you enjoy being visible in the business, building trusted relationships and delivering practical HR solutions, this is an opportunity to make a tangible impact.

job.title: Employee & Industrial Relations Lead
job.description:
About Them
Join a large, values-driven organisation that provides critical services to communities across New South Wales.
With a highly skilled workforce operating across metropolitan, regional and remote locations, the organisation plays an important role supporting individuals through some of life's most challenging circumstances. Their work is diverse, fast-paced and deeply connected to the communities they serve.
Following a period of transformation within the People & Culture function, the organisation continues to invest in strengthening its Employment and Industrial Relations capability to support a changing workforce and evolving operational environment.

About the Role
Reporting into an experienced and credible Industrial Relations leader, this role sits at the centre of some of the organisation's most complex and high-profile people matters.
You'll act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, providing expert ER and IR advice across a broad portfolio of workforce issues. The role offers a genuine mix of operational and strategic work, with a strong focus on organisational change, employee relations and stakeholder management.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Providing expert advice across ER and IR matters
  • Managing complex investigations, grievances and workplace conduct issues
  • Supporting leaders through organisational restructures and workforce change initiatives
  • Partnering with unions and employee representatives
  • Supporting conflict resolution and workplace risk management
  • Contributing to strategic ER and IR projects across the organisation
  • Interpreting industrial instruments, policies and employment legislation
This is not a transactional case management role. The work is varied, complex and often unique, offering exposure to matters rarely seen in more traditional commercial environments.

About You
You are an experienced Employee Relations or Industrial Relations professional who thrives in complex, fast-paced environments and enjoys partnering with leaders to navigate sensitive workplace matters. You bring a strong foundation in ER and IR, with hands-on experience managing investigations, grievances, misconduct matters and workplace conflict. You have supported organisational change initiatives, including restructures and consultation processes, and are confident engaging with unions and employee representatives. With a sound understanding of Australian employment legislation and industrial frameworks, you provide pragmatic, commercially minded advice while balancing risk, stakeholder needs and organisational outcomes. Strong relationship-building skills, sound judgement and the ability to influence at all levels will be key to your success in this role.

Public sector experience will be highly regarded, however candidates from other complex, unionised environments are encouraged to apply.
 
You'll join a fun, collaborative and supportive team, work alongside respected leaders in the field, and gain exposure to significant organisational change initiatives.

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, the HR Lead will take ownership of the full HR function and lead a small HR team - a Recruitment Coordinator and HR & WHS Coordinator. Key responsibilities will include:
  • Develop and implement a HR strategy aligned to the organisation's growth and business objectives
  • Partner closely with the Managing Director and senior leadership team on people priorities
  • Lead, coach and develop the existing HR team
  • Provide trusted advice and support across employee relations, performance management and workplace matters
  • Strengthen performance management, capability development and leadership practices
  • Oversee recruitment and onboarding, ensuring a strong candidate and employee experience
  • Drive employee engagement, recognition and retention initiatives
  • Review and enhance HR policies, processes and systems
  • Ensure strong employment compliance and sound HR governance
  • Oversee WHS in partnership with the WHS & HR Coordinator
  • Identify opportunities to improve HR systems (Employment Hero), reporting, use of AI, and people data
  • Develop training and development initiatives across the business
  • Support the continued development of a positive, connected and high-performing culture
This is a role where you will be encouraged to look at what is working, identify where things can be improved and make meaningful change.

About You

You will be an experienced HR professional with leadership experience who enjoys operating across both the strategic and hands-on sides of HR.
You will bring:
  • Proven experience in an HR leadership, HR Manager or senior HR partnering role
  • Strong knowledge of Australian employment legislation and contemporary HR practices
  • Experience working across employee relations, performance, recruitment, engagement and compliance
  • The ability to confidently coach and influence managers and senior leaders
  • A practical, commercially minded approach to HR
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • The confidence to operate autonomously and take ownership of the HR agenda
  • A continuous improvement mindset and an interest in building better people processes
  • The ability to balance strategic thinking with being comfortable rolling up your sleeves and getting things done
Importantly, you will be someone who genuinely cares about people. You will be approachable and authentic, while also having the confidence to provide clear, commercially sound advice when it matters.

Experience within a multi-site, retail, hospitality, service or other operationally focused environment is important. 

About Culture & Benefits

This is an opportunity to join a business with a passionate and caring Founder/Managing Director who is genuinely invested in the people and culture of the organisation.

Based at their Head Office in the Logan/Brisbane south corridor, this is an opportunity to join a business where HR is valued as an important part of the broader commercial strategy and where you will have genuine influence across the organisation.

You will have:
  • Genuine ownership of the HR function and the opportunity to shape its future direction
  • Direct exposure and partnership with the Managing Director and senior leadership team
  • The opportunity to lead and develop an existing HR team
  • A broad and varied HR remit across a national, multi-site workforce
  • The opportunity to make a visible impact across an organisation of approximately 350 employees
  • A modern, engaging office environment where you are immersed in the broader operation - with the corporate office, design hub, warehouse and distribution centre all located together
  • A collaborative, down-to-earth and people-focused culture
  • Weekly Friday afternoon team connection gatherings 
  • Offering a highly competitive salary
